message.content:
Below is a quick‑look at the **long weekends** that Canadians will enjoy in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” here means a holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday, giving you a three‑day break.  Some holidays are provincial/territorial, so the exact dates may differ depending on where you live.)

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 1–3** | New Year’s Day (Observed Jan 2) | New Year’s Day falls on Sunday, so the following Monday (Jan 2) is a statutory holiday. |
| **Feb 18–20** | Family Day (Ontario, BC, AB, SK, MB, NB, PEI, NS, NL) | Observed on the third Monday of February. |
| **Apr 7–9** | Good Friday (and Easter Monday for some provinces) | Good Friday is a statutory holiday; Easter Monday is a holiday in some provinces. |
| **May 22–24** | Victoria Day (all provinces) | Celebrated on the last Monday before May 25. |
| **Sep 4–6** | Labour Day (all provinces) | First Monday in September. |
| **Oct 9–11** | Thanksgiving (all provinces) | Second Monday in October. |
| **Dec 25–27** | Christmas & Boxing Day (all provinces) | Christmas on Monday, Boxing Day on Tuesday. |

> **Pro tip:** If you’re planning trips around a holiday that falls on a Wednesday or Thursday, you can often “bridge” the gap by taking a day off on either side (e.g., take Friday off to extend a Wednesday holiday).

Feel free to plug these dates into your holiday‑planning app!
